label: Bible Study
prompt: Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above _____.
verse: Who can find a virtuous woman? for her price is far above rubies.
note: The opening line of the virtuous woman poem — an acrostic running through the Hebrew alphabet.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: He giveth power to the _____; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength.
verse: He giveth power to the faint; and to them that have no might he increaseth strength.
note: Strength for the faint, power for the powerless — two verses before the famous eagles' wings.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And Jesus answering said unto them, _____ to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's. And they marvelled at him.
verse: And Jesus answering said unto them, Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's. And they marvelled at him.
note: 'Render' is the KJV's word for 'give back' — Caesar's coin to Caesar, God's image to God.

label: Deep Water
prompt: And it shall come to pass at that time, that I will search Jerusalem with _____, and punish the men that are settled on their lees: that say in their heart, The LORD will not do good, neither will he do evil.
verse: And it shall come to pass at that time, that I will search Jerusalem with candles, and punish the men that are settled on their lees: that say in their heart, The LORD will not do good, neither will he do evil.
note: God combs Jerusalem by lamplight for the complacent — 'settled on their lees' is wine left too long on its dregs.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: Because _____ is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.
verse: Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.
note: 'Strait' means tight and narrow, as in straitjacket — not 'straight.' The KJV gate is cramped, not level.
